item.title: Billie Jean King changed women’s tennis. A new documentary shows what it cost her
item.description: “Give Me the Ball!” the ESPN's 30 for 30 documentary chronicling Billie Jean King, emphasizes the sports legend’s love of competition by showcasing just how much she sacrificed for it. King, who won 39 Grand Slam titles and a record 20 Wimbledon titles, dealt with multiple personal struggles surrounding her identity and sexuality as she used her status as a world No. 1 player to blaze the trail for equal pay for women in tennis. “My whole life, I’ve been trying to be No. 1 in the world,” King says in the opening sequence of the documentary, which centers on her defeat of Bobby Riggs in the 1973 “Battle of the Sexes” match. “When I was very young, I just loved sports. I loved playing. I loved winning,” before teeing up the documentary’s title. “It didn’t matter if it was a football, a tennis ball, a softball, a baseball — give me the ball.” After discovering tennis through free lessons in her native Southern California, King said she quickly learned the history of the sport and began to idolize Althea Gibson; one of the first Black athletes to cross the color line of international tennis and first Black player to win a Grand Slam event. Decades later, King broke her own barrier as she became the first prominent active professional female athlete to publicly come out as gay, but not without great turmoil. “How did I survive?” King reflected in the film while describing 1973 as the most pivotal year in women’s tennis but one of the most difficult times in her life. “(I was) trying to be No. 1, trying to help women’s sports, trying to get the players together, trying to make a living, trying to get equal prize money, trying to get a sponsor, trying to get a divorce, trying to make everybody happy, trying to figure out who I am – the sexuality part — trying to avoid it, trying to do damage control, trying to change society,” King said. “Oh yeah, I gotta play tennis, too.” Billie Jean King documentary examines abortion, affair In 1971, King opted to have an abortion, a choice publicized against her will by her then-husband Larry King. She said her husband encouraged her to get off birth control for health reasons and assured her she wouldn’t get pregnant. At the time, her husband's signature was required to be granted the abortion. King was later asked about the abortion during a “60 Minutes” interview even though she’d asked for it not to be mentioned — which led to emotional fallout with her mother, who King had not told about her choice. “It wasn’t good,” King said. “It was very difficult.” The documentary introduced King’s former husband as a “feminist” with whom she fell in love during college. The couple detailed how they grew apart as King’s career continued to take off and his desire for a family intensified. “It wasn’t right for Larry and I to stay married because I didn’t know what I was doing. Hadn’t figured out who I was. And he shouldn’t be suffering through that either,” King said. “I kept pleading with him to divorce me and he wouldn’t.”

item.title: I’ll continue to criticise Atiku for attacking Tinubu – Shettima
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Vice-President Kashim Shettima has defended his right to criticise African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, saying he would not hold back in defending President Bola Tinubu against political attacks. Shettima, who described Atiku as an elder statesman whom he holds in high regard, said their political differences would not prevent him from expressing his views about the former vice-president. He spoke on Tuesday in Maiduguri, Borno State’s capital, during the inauguration of the North-East Development Commission’s multi-sectoral development interventions. “We respect former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar. He is an elder statesman we hold in very high esteem, but as a Fulani man, I have the right to throw stones at him. And he has to endure strictly whatever stones I throw at him,” he said. The vice president also cautioned against attempts to portray political disagreements as personal hostility, saying he was willing to maintain cordial relationships with opposition figures as long as they did not attack his principal. “So long as they do not attack my boss, we will practise politics of maturity, politics without bitterness, and politics of tolerance because what binds us together surpasses whatever that divides us,” he said. Shettima also identified former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi and former Kano State Governor Rabiu Kwankwaso as his friends, while describing Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde as a personal friend. He said he had never insulted Makinde, adding that political differences should not undermine relationships among leaders. The vice-president urged Nigerians to make informed decisions ahead of the 2027 presidential election, arguing that the Tinubu administration’s economic policies were beginning to yield results. Shettima also ruled out a return to petrol subsidy, saying its removal and the realignment of multiple exchange rates were necessary to prevent the economy from collapsing. “The president has a great deal of human empathy for the Nigerian people. He withdrew the subsidy, not to inflict pain on Nigerians. No, he removed the subsidy to save the Nigerian economy from collapse,” he said. He further accused some Nigerians who had benefited from the previous economic arrangements of sponsoring anti-government sentiments. Calling for restraint among political actors, Shettima urged candidates to accept the outcome of the 2027 election rather than resort to threats and actions capable of creating tension. He expressed confidence that Nigerians would vote massively for Tinubu on January 16, adding that there were no polling booths on Facebook, Instagram or other social media platforms. item.title: Senegal re-crowned Afcon champions after appeal upheld
item.description: Senegal have been re-crowned the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations champions after the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) unanimously upheld their appeal against the decision to strip them of their title on Tuesday. Senegal contested Confederation of African Football's (Caf) decision to declare Morocco champions , wiping the Teranga Lions’ title from the records despite winning January’s Afcon final 1-0 after extra time in Rabat. The final was fraught with controversy after Senegal staged a walk-off in protest to an injury-time penalty was awarded against them in the dying stages of normal time, with players ordered into the dressing room by manager Pape Thiaw , where they remained for 14 minutes. Play was eventually resumed before Morocco’s Brahim Diaz missed the spot-kick, sailing a tame ‘Panenka’ effort into the arms of Edouard Mendy. Senegal went on to win the match in extra time through Pape Gueye. Brahim Diaz missed the penalty after Senegal staged a 14-minute walk-off (AFP/Getty) However, they were stripped of the title two months later after Caf’s Appeal Board ruled that Senegal had forfeited ⁠the match by walking off the pitch, overturning the result and awarding a 3-0 ​victory to ⁠Morocco. Senegal quickly followed with an appeal to sport's highest court, Cas, which was lodged on 25 March and have now successfully fought their case to be reinstated as champions, with the original 1-0 result restored. The three-man Cas ‌panel, presided over by French sports law ​expert Gerald Simon with assistance from ‌Italian international law professor ⁠Luigi Fumagalli and Hamburg-based ⁠attorney Ulrich Haas, ‌unanimously found that referee Jean-Jacques Ndala “did not commit any error of law”, said Cas secretary general Matthieu Reeb. Ndala’s decision to resume the match after Senegal’s walk-off fell within his sole authority and was therefore covered by the “field of play” doctrine, something Morocco’s federation argued was not the case. The court published its reasoning in a press release issued on Tuesday afternoon, which read: “By blowing his whistle to restart play, the referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met – both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume. “In the panel’s view, there is no doubt that the effects of the referee’s decision were limited to the pitch.” The panel clarified that Articles 82 and 84 of Caf’s tournament regulations, cited in the Moroccan federation’s appeal, apply only to determining match results if team conduct forces a referee to permanently call off a game, and were therefore not applicable in this instance. "In conclusion, the panel considers that in resuming the match, the referee did not err in law," a court press release added. item.description: Mandatory Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images Los Angeles Lakers guard Cameron Carr saw his lifelong dream come true in 2026 as he finally made it to the NBA. Never had NBA League Pass. So that s***’s great… They do the Sleep Number stuff for the rookies. Like a discount code or something. That’s great… I’m a big sleep guy. Like, as soon as I get done with this, I’m gonna shower, go home, and take a nap.” The base version of the NBA League Pass costs $109.99 for an entire season in the U.S., while the premium one is $159.99. Carr signed a four-year, $16.8 million rookie-scale contract with the Lakers, but still views the free League Pass as a great perk because he never had it before. The 22-year-old also greatly appreciates getting a discount code for Sleep Number, the smart mattress brand. Carr saying he’s a “big sleep guy” might sound funny, but sleep is extremely important for athletes. It’s as vital as nutrition and training. Not sleeping right adversely affects an athlete’s performance, and it’s great that Carr recognizes its importance. His father, Chris Carr, is a former NBA player and might have provided guidance on this matter. The elder Carr was a journeyman who played six seasons in the NBA, and the younger one could potentially have a far better career. item.title: Cameron Smith wants PGA Tour return after LIV Golf collapse, but road back won’t be easy
item.description: Cameron Smith wants back on the PGA Tour. Getting there, however, could be the hard part. The 2022 British Open champion acknowledged Tuesday that the PGA Tour is where he wants to play again, even as current Tour players have made it clear they aren't interested in rolling out the red carpet for LIV Golf defectors looking to return. “(The PGA Tour) is where I want to be now, for sure,” Smith told the Sydney Morning Herald . “There’s plenty of good players out there and plenty of other guys that want to do the same thing, so it’s going to be difficult.” Smith’s change of direction comes after the collapse of LIV Golf. The Saudi-backed league is shutting down and liquidating its remaining assets after B.C. Partners backed out of a proposed $300 million investment designed to keep LIV afloat and fund a restructuring. And if former LIV players were hoping their PGA Tour peers might be sympathetic to their predicament, the early indications suggest otherwise. News of LIV’s demise broke during the PGA Tour’s World Wide Technology Championship at El Cardonal at Diamante, an event that moved to Los Cabos after former host Mayakoba Resort partnered with LIV. Among the PGA Tour players competing there, there wasn’t much sympathy for those suddenly looking for a way back. Erik van Rooyen summed up his feelings in four words: “Go back to Q-school.” “We were told initially that if you played LIV, you would be banned from the PGA Tour, and the story just kept changing,” van Rooyen said. “They gave the finger to the Tour. If you’re that good, go get it done.” Smith’s situation is particularly interesting because he already had an opportunity to return. He was one of four players eligible for the PGA Tour’s hastily created Returning Member Program in January. Brooks Koepka took advantage of that pathway, which included a $5 million charitable donation and the loss of player equity participation for five years. Smith, Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm opted to remain with LIV. Now Smith has to find another way back. With former LIV players facing a one-year PGA Tour ban from the date of their most recent LIV appearance, Smith is turning to the DP World Tour to begin rebuilding his career. DeChambeau and Rahm have committed to full DP World Tour schedules next season, while Smith is among nine former LIV players who signed agreements giving them invitations to a specific number of DP World Tour events. Smith’s comeback begins Thursday in Sydney at the BMW Australian PGA Championship, the opening event of the DP World Tour’s new season. There is plenty of work to do. Smith was one of the best players in the world when he left for LIV, but he hasn’t come close to maintaining that form. item.title: Senegal reinstated as Afcon 2025 winners by court ruling
item.description: Sadio Mane's Senegal have been confirmed as Afcon 2025 winners following their appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport, giving the Teranga Lions a second continental title [Getty Images] Senegal have been reinstated as winners of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) after a ruling by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas). The court's award overturns a previous decision which had stripped the West Africans of the title they won on the pitch during a chaotic final against host nation Morocco in January. The result of that match in Rabat, which saw the Teranga Lions triumph 1-0 after extra time, was overturned almost two months later when a Confederation of African Football (Caf) appeals board decreed Senegal had breached competition regulations by leaving the field of play in second-half stoppage time in protest at a penalty awarded against them. Senegal's football federation (FSF) subsequently appealed to Cas, sport's highest legal authority, with a three-man panel hearing its case behind closed doors in Lausanne on 8 October. In a unanimous verdict, the Cas panel has effectively backed the decision by referee Jean-Jacques Ndala to restart the game after Senegal returned to the field and the match was played to a conclusion. The result of the final stands and Senegal are now confirmed as Afcon 2025 winners. The court said it considered that "the referee's decision to resume the match or to stop it fell definitively within his sole authority". "By blowing his whistle to restart play, the referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met - both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume." The FSF immediately reacted with a social media post featuring a picture of the side lifting the trophy in January captioned with the phrase "again and always". Caf is yet to comment on the decision but its president Patrice Motsepe has repeatedly said that his organisation will respect and adhere to the Cas ruling. Morocco's football federation (FRMF) is also yet to comment on the verdict. 'Shameful' and 'terrible look' - the chaos that marred Afcon 2025 final 'The longest VAR check in history' - the fallout from shock Afcon decision Morocco and Senegal have both changed coach since the final and earlier this month secured their places at the 2027 edition of the tournament with two rounds of qualification remaining. This ruling should now settle any debate about who the history books will recognise as continental champions - although plenty in Morocco may not agree with the outcome of the case at Cas. item.description: Mandatory Credit: Daniel Dunn-Imagn Images We’ve seen enough from the San Antonio Spurs this season to know they remain the same championship contenders as last year. They’re 15-3 after beating the Kings 123-107 on Monday, Victor Wembanyama is having an MVP-caliber season , and the backcourt of De’Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle has been working very well. But the Spurs have also lost Dylan Harper to a left hip injury , while Tobias Harris is still waiting to make his season debut due to a left calf strain. And with the way this team has started the season, I wouldn’t be surprised if the front office looked for some help before the trade deadline . One team I’d call right now is the Los Angeles Clippers , who are 4-12 and 13th in the Western Conference after losing 116-104 to the Rockets on Monday. They have some veterans who could help other teams, including Derrick Jones Jr . and Brook Lopez , who’s somehow having one of his best offensive seasons in years at 38 years old. The Spurs have enough players and draft assets to put together an offer without touching their young stars, so let’s see how a trade for both Clippers veterans could work. The Spurs would send around $23.6 million in salaries between their three players, with the final deal depending on the Clippers’ salary-cap restrictions. The 2028 first-round pick comes from the Derrick White deal back in 2022, as the Spurs have swap rights involving the Celtics’ selection in 2028. The idea would be to give the Clippers a young prospect, future draft compensation, and a center under contract for several more years, while the Spurs get two players who could help them win right now. item.title: Freddy Peralta Predicted To Sign With Rays Over Blue Jays, Cubs, Other Suitors
item.description: Free agent pitcher Freddy Peralta Freddy Peralta is the top remaining starting pitcher on the open market, and there are a few teams that have been linked to him. According to The Athletic's Ken Rosenthal and Will Sammon , the Tampa Bay Rays, Chicago Cubs, Chicago White Sox, Toronto Blue Jays and San Diego Padres are known suitors for Peralta. Bleacher Report's Erik Beaston predicted the Rays would re-sign him. "While there will be big-money opportunities elsewhere, the Rays are a team set up to run it back in the AL and compete for another World Series," wrote Beaston. "The other teams mentioned are still a few pieces away, even with Peralta. That could prove to be a deciding factor in where the 30-year-old continues his career." The Rays are not known as huge spenders, but they could make an exception for Peralta, who was phenomenal for them. Peralta is viewed as the top priority for the Blue Jays, per MLB Network's Jom Morosi . The Cubs have had "extensive talks" with him, per USA Today's Bob Nightengale . The Padres were one of the teams involved in the Skubal sweepstakes, and the White Sox are in desperate need of starting pitching. However, the Rays have the inside edge when it comes to Peralta. Peralta has already said he wants to return to the Rays. The Cubs have already agreed to a deal with Trevor Rogers, so they may not be as aggressive in pursuit of Peralta. However, the Blue Jays, Padres and White Sox still have plenty of reasons to try to get him. There may be more teams trying to get him as well, but among the known suitors, the Rays could have a leg up. item.description: The New York Giants helped themselves immensely in the race to the NFC East title with their 23-18 victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday. Unfortunately for the Giants, the rest of the division kept pace. The 5-6 Dallas Cowboys overwhelmed the hapless Tennessee Titans, the Philadelphia Eagles upset the Pittsburgh Steelers, and perhaps most importantly in the big picture the Washington Commanders upset the Cincinnati Bengals 22-20 on Monday Night Football. item.title: Senegal regain AFCON title after appeal to sports court
item.description: Sadio Mane holds up the AFCON trophy after Senegal's 1-0 extra-time win over hosts Morocco in the final in January (SEBASTIEN BOZON) Senegal on Tuesday regained their Africa Cup of Nations title after winning an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) against the decision by the Confederation of African Football to declare Morocco the winners following a chaotic final in January. "The Court of Arbitration for Sport has upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF) concerning the final of the Africa Cup of Nations Morocco 2025," CAS said in a statement. The Swiss-based sports court said Senegal's appeal had been upheld by "a unanimous decision", and their original 1-0 victory after extra time is reinstated. In March, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) sensationally overturned the result of the final, awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory, and the title, after many Senegalese players walked off the pitch in protest at a penalty given to the hosts with the game still goalless. The CAF Appeals Committee had justified its decision to overturn the result and declare Morocco champions based on Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations. Those state that if a team "refuses to play or leaves the ground before the regular end of the match without the authorisation of the referee, it shall be considered (loser) and shall be eliminated for good from the current competition". However, the Senegal players eventually returned to the pitch and the final carried on. The CAS panel therefore considered that the referee's decision to restart the final showed that "the conditions for resuming the match had been met", and that articles 82 and 84 were therefore "not applicable in this case". elm-obo/dar/as/mw

item.title: Red Wings Chaos Delayed Larkin Deal
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect According to Dylan Larkin’s agent, the chaos that erupted within the Detroit Red Wings organization over the summer months derailed any hope of an early resolution to Larkin’s trade request. Appearing on Sportsnet, Pat Brisson acknowledged that Larkin first issued his trade demand to the Red Wings in May. "Teams were calling the Red Wings when no one was in charge… It was a very frustrating process." Dylan Larkin's agent, Pat Brisson, joins @RealKyper and @jtbourne to go behind the scenes on the deal. pic.twitter.com/mXshuYfOtT — Sportsnet (@Sportsnet) November 23, 2026 “Once we made it official in May when Dylan requested a trade, we’re hoping for this to happen before the draft because it’s always a better time of the year for these things to happen,” Brisson said. “A lot of moving parts. “That’s when teams are rebuilt for the most part. And then once we passed July 1st and Steve [ Yzerman ] was let go [as GM] on July 14th, it made it very, very complicated for us and for Detroit to operate. “Teams were calling the Red Wings with offers, and there was no one in charge officially.” Red Wings Summer of Discontent Put Larkin in Limbo While the Red Wings fiddled over their future direction throughout the summer, Brisson and Larkin were left to stew on the sideline. And any chance for a quick resolution to what became a festering sore for the Red Wings was gone. “It was a very frustrating process because July and August were two dead months, so to speak,” Brisson said. “I was hoping that at that point they’d have a leadership group in place so we could have had conversations and progressive conversations in order to try to get it done. “But it didn’t happen.” Instead, the Red Wings waited until the eve of training camp in September to install Shawn Horcoff as interim GM. “Shawn Horcoff only became the interim GM two days before camp in September,” Brisson said. “It’s a very tough time to move an asset because teams are ready for camp. They want to try their young guys. They’re fulfilled. “Everyone’s winning the Cup at that time.” Instead, it took until Sunday, November 22, to finally resolve Larkin’s request when he was dealt to the Montreal Canadiens. Seven months after his request was initially made. item.title: How would a deal like Tarik Skubal’s work under a salary cap?
item.description: Last week at the MLB owners meetings, Commissioner Rob Manfred said this : “I can’t imagine the owners ratifying a deal that does not include a cap and floor.” Okay. So that’s probably posturing and not what’s actually going to happen whenever MLB owners and the MLBPA reach a deal. But it’s out there. So let’s look at some things that could happen going forward. At Forbes, Maury Brown has written about what a deal like the one Tarik Skubal has agreed to with the Mets might do under such a cap/floor system, and the problem is summed up this way: Under MLB’s latest economic proposal, a salary cap and floor system would start in 2028. Accounting for present-day values, eight players would consume 92% of the Mets’ cap allocation for that year. It remains unknown how multi-year contracts extending past 2028 would be handled if a cap is implemented. So there’s the issue in a nutshell. Not every team has contracts like the Skubal deal, or the Juan Soto deal also eating up a lot of the Mets’ payroll, but what would happen going forward where contracts like that would push a team way over any cap proposal? Brown writes about two ways things could go for MLB. First, he mentions the NHL and how they lost an entire season arguing about a salary cap, which was eventually instituted. And before you say that can’t happen in MLB — yes, it absolutely could. Here’s what happened in the NHL: To start, all remaining contracts were rolled back 24% for the 2004-05 season. Contracts on the books after that were simply voided. Additionally, the rollback also hit players who had to be given qualifying offers for new deals. Those qualifying offers were based on a player’s salary in his last contracted year, minus the 24% rollback. This seems like an extraordinary leap for MLB players to make, but it does show that a rollback has been done in the past. I believe Brown is correct that this would be “an extraordinary leap for MLB players to make.” The other way is to grandfather pre-cap contracts, as the NBA did when they instituted their cap system. That worked this way: One scenario would be for all existing multiyear contracts past 2028 to be honored, likely with the league moving off a hard cap and to a soft cap. This follows what the NBA did in 2005: contracts signed prior to the new deal were honored as written—there were no rollbacks or voids to existing salaries. The NBA also allowed for contracts of four or more seasons to be renegotiated (for teams under the cap) after the third anniversary of signing, extending, or a prior renegotiation that raised any season’s salary by more than 8%, while contracts under four years could not be renegotiated. To me, this would seem the most likely scenario. It also would explain why Steve Cohen lavished that contract on Skubal. item.title: Never mind the quarterbacks — Patriots must improve their defense to make the playoffs
item.description: When you’re tethered to bad quarterback play in the NFL, it can seem like a hopeless endeavor. While all the cool kids are out there making effortless big plays with the likes of Joe Burrow, Josh Allen, Trevor Lawrence, and Brock Purdy, those kids stuck at the end of the playground need to level up for any chance. And unfortunately, this is the position the Patriots find themselves in as long as Drake Maye is out with the fractured fibula he suffered in last Sunday’s 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions . The other quarterbacks on the Patriots’ depth chart — Tommy “Cutlets” DeVito and rookie Behren Morton — are not ready for primetime, and DeVito proved his part of that in the Lions game. He completed 12 of 24 passes for 81 yards, one touchdown, one interception, a passer rating of 54.3, and an EPA per dropback of -0.55, which was the NFL’s fifth-worst in Week 10. Even when DeVito connected with his receivers, those completions were too often “cemetery balls,” throws that led receivers straight into converging defenders. tommy devito oof madon' pic.twitter.com/2jvMN7G9Po — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) November 18, 2026 It’s unrealistic to expect DeVito to become something he’s not for the rest of the 2026 season, even with the Week 11 bye that gives him an extra week to prepare. And because Maye’s injury happened after the Nov. 10 trade deadline (something I’ve proposed that the league should extend for situations like this ), New England’s options are limited. So, do the Patriots punt on the season at 5-5? Certainly not, but how do they get past a clear deficit at the game’s most important position? item.title: 2026 Dodgers season review: Max Muncy
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 21: Max Muncy #13 of the Los Angeles Dodgers celebrates his two run home run, to take a 2-1 lead over the Pittsburgh Pirates, during the first inning at Dodger Stadium on August 21, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images An underrated aspect of how the Dodgers have managed to stay at and near the top for so long is how their veteran players seem to age so gracefully. And perhaps, no player better embodies that than Max Muncy, who shows no signs of slowing down at 36 years of age, coming off one of his better seasons in a long time. It’s not only because he’s been healthier, setting a new career high in games played with 149, but also because he’s still with top-notch production, near the top of the team’s leaderboards in most offensive categories. On a per-rate basis, Muncy was coming off productive campaigns, but injuries limited him to just 86.5 games per season between 2024 and 2025. It was a different story this past season, as one of the more reliable hitters on the top team was in the top 3 in both runs scored (81) and RBI (76). Interestingly, while Pages took advantage of Ohtani’s down year with the bat to accomplish an unlikely feat in leading the team in RBI, Muncy had a similar opportunity with the long ball. However, the veteran fell just shy of it with 29 homers, one fewer than Ohtani. Early in the year, though, Muncy was all about the multihomer game, noting that three of the first four games he left the yard in were all multihomer games—including a three-homer day against the Rangers, one you’ll read more about in the Game of the Year section. Surprisingly, it was only Muncy’s second three-homer game and first one in nearly two years, repeating a feat he first accomplished against the Braves in 2024. Those multihomer games laid the foundation for what would be a productive season, but they often came with a minimized impact, as each of Muncy’s first eight home runs were all solo shots—helping explain why he entered May with more extra-base hits (13) than RBI (11). An impressive first half helped Muncy earn his third All-Star appearance, but more importantly, the first one as a starter, beating Alec Bohm in the process. Not short of talent at the position in recent years, it had been a while since the Dodgers last sent the starter at third to the All-Star game, nearly half a century. Prior to Muncy, Ron Cey, in 1977, was the last Dodger third baseman to feature in the starting lineup for the NL in an All-Star Game. As if to celebrate this achievement, Muncy returned for the second half with one of his most impactful games of the regular season, securing a homer and two-RBI in the Dodgers’ narrow 2-1 victory over the Yankees. Taking Gerrit Cole deep in the 7th inning of a game in which your team trails 1-0 in the meeting of baseball’s two biggest franchises is a special moment, even for a veteran. item.title: Senate orders scrutiny of revised 2025 laws
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate has called for a thorough scrutiny of the revised and consolidated Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2025, to ensure accuracy before granting legislative approval. The President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio, made the call on Tuesday while reading a letter from President Bola Tinubu seeking the National Assembly’s approval of the revised compendium. Akpabio said the Senate must ensure that all amendments were accurately reflected and that no provisions had been altered from the original laws passed by the National Assembly. He said it was necessary to compare the compiled laws with the versions passed by both chambers to prevent discrepancies that could undermine the country’s legal framework. In the letter, Tinubu said the committee constituted on October 24, 2024, examined 932 federal enactments and 731 subsidiary legislations. He disclosed that 664 principal enactments were validated for inclusion in the revised compendium, while 268 were identified as obsolete, spent or repealed. According to the President, the updated compendium would provide a reliable legal reference for the judiciary, legal practitioners, government institutions, investors and the general public. The Senate subsequently referred the revised compendium to the Committees on Rules and Business and Judiciary for further legislative action. Contributing to the debate, former Senate Leader, Senator Yahaya Abdullahi (APC, Kebbi North), described the exercise as important to Nigeria’s legal system and the administration of justice. He recalled that a similar exercise was conducted after the return to democratic governance in 1999 to give legitimacy to decrees enacted under military administrations. Abdullahi, who noted that the last official consolidation of the laws was undertaken in 2004, said the current exercise had become necessary after more than two decades. He, however, cautioned against rushing the process, given its implications for the country’s legal system and justice delivery. He proposed that the compendium be thoroughly examined by the Senate Committee on Judiciary, Human Rights and Legal Matters, with the support of competent legal experts. According to him, the committee should analyse the volumes and present a comprehensive report to enable lawmakers to understand the proposed changes before approval. Also contributing, Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Jibrin Barau (APC, Kano North), supported the call for scrutiny, warning that even a single altered clause could make the compilation inconsistent with the laws passed by the National Assembly. item.title: UniCredit Opens Bitcoin to Italian Savers, Capping Gains at 65%
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine UniCredit Opens Bitcoin to Italian Savers, Capping Gains at 65% UniCredit on Tuesday began selling a capital-protected certificate that lets retail clients in Italy follow the bitcoin price, a product the bank calls the first investment solution of its kind in the country. The six-year, euro-denominated certificate will be listed on the Munich stock exchange and is linked to the iShares Bitcoin ETP managed by BlackRock, UniCredit said in a release. The placement period runs from Nov. 24 to Dec. 18, 2026. The note is open only to UniCredit Italia retail clients with specific characteristics, and only through the bank’s advisory service. It can’t be bought independently or by investors who aren’t UniCredit clients, and the minimum investment is €1,000, Italian newswire Teleborsa reported . How the certificate works A capital-protected certificate is a structured note. The issuing bank promises to repay the original investment at maturity and pays a return tied to an underlying asset, in this case bitcoin through the BlackRock product. Buyers hold a claim on the bank, not bitcoin itself. If bitcoin is down at maturity, holders get 100% of their capital back. If it rises, they share in the gain up to a maximum return of 65% on the capital invested. Before maturity, the certificate’s price follows market conditions, so the protection applies only at the end of the six years. That cap works out to roughly 8.7% a year at most, no matter how far bitcoin climbs. And because the certificate is UniCredit’s own debt, the protection depends on the bank’s ability to pay. Documents for a similar UniCredit note in Germany state that no third-party guarantee covers an issuer default. “With the launch of this certificate, UniCredit is writing a new page of financial innovation in the country, confirming its market leadership,” said Chicco Di Stasi, Head of Group Investment Product Solutions at UniCredit. “Diversification is no longer just a prudential rule, but the key to capturing the value of the future,” Di Stasi said, adding that the bank is responding to growing client demand and offering the product to Italian savers “for the very first time.” Built on notes sold in Germany and Austria Di Stasi said the bank is bringing to Italy “a pioneering model already proven by its success in Germany and Austria.” Those earlier notes are denominated in dollars and track BlackRock’s U.S.-listed iShares Bitcoin Trust instead. HypoVereinsbank, UniCredit’s German unit, sold a version to private clients in March with a 160% cap, or 60% upside. UniCredit Bank Austria launched its own six-year note in April with a 175% cap, or 75% upside. Italy’s 65% falls between the two. The bank has moved into bitcoin in steps. item.description: By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has passed two bills seeking to reform Nigeria’s social investment programmes and strengthen the regulation of optometry and dispensing opticians through second reading. The bills, sponsored by Deputy Speaker Benjamin Kalu and other lawmakers, are aimed at improving the delivery of social protection programmes and addressing regulatory gaps in the country’s eye care sector. Leading the debate on the proposed amendment to the National Social Investment Programme Agency (Establishment) Act, 2023, Kalu said the success of social investment programmes should be measured not by the size of their budgets or the number of initiatives introduced, but by their actual impact on vulnerable Nigerians. He described social investment as a commitment by the Nigerian state to prevent temporary hardship from becoming permanent exclusion. The Deputy Speaker said the growing scale and complexity of Nigeria’s social protection system had made it necessary to strengthen the institutional framework for coordinating, implementing and monitoring interventions. According to him, the proposed amendment would address administrative fragmentation, duplication of beneficiaries, unreliable data and inadequate coordination among the different levels of government. Among its major provisions is the introduction of the Grant for Vulnerable Groups Programme and the National Social Safety-Net Coordinating Office as components of the agency. The bill also seeks to establish the National Social Safety-Net Coordinating Office as the central institution for coordinating and managing data on national social safety nets, including maintaining, updating and verifying the National Social Register. Kalu said the proposed legislation would also provide for the establishment of state offices to bring programme implementation closer to beneficiaries and introduce executive directors with clearly defined responsibilities for individual programmes. He explained that the changes would strengthen accountability, improve coordination and ensure that government assistance reached intended beneficiaries. He identified children requiring support to remain in school, unemployed youths seeking economic opportunities and vulnerable households needing temporary assistance as some of those expected to benefit from a more coordinated social investment system. item.title: Senegal Regain AFCON Title After Appeal
item.description: Senegal on Tuesday regained their Africa Cup of Nations title after winning an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) against the decision by the Confederation of African Football to declare Morocco the winners following a chaotic final in January. “The Court of Arbitration for Sport has upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF) concerning the final of the Africa Cup of Nations Morocco 2025,” CAS said in a statement. The Swiss-based sports court said Senegal’s appeal had been upheld by “a unanimous decision”, and their original 1-0 victory after extra time is reinstated. In March, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) sensationally overturned the result of the final, awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory, and the title, after many Senegalese players walked off the pitch in protest at a penalty given to the hosts with the game still goalless. Senegal and Morocco players line up prior the Africa Cup of Nations (CAN) final football match between Senegal and Morocco at the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium in Rabat on January 18, 2026. Photo by PAUL ELLIS / AFP The CAF Appeals Committee had justified its decision to overturn the result and declare Morocco champions based on Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations. Those state that if a team “refuses to play or leaves the ground before the regular end of the match without the authorisation of the referee, it shall be considered (loser) and shall be eliminated for good from the current competition”. However, the Senegal players eventually returned to the pitch and the final carried on. The CAS panel therefore considered that the referee’s decision to restart the final showed that “the conditions for resuming the match had been met”, and that articles 82 and 84 were therefore “not applicable in this case”. item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The Kabiru Tanimu Turaki-led Interim National Working Committee (INWC) of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has blamed President Bola Tinubu’s past political statements for what it described as a growing climate of violence against opposition parties, following the killing of at least four persons in an attack on a Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) campaign in Delta State. The group said the attack in Uduere, Ughelli North, where gunmen opened fire while former Deputy Senate President and NDC Delta Central senatorial candidate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, was addressing supporters, exposed the dangers of inflammatory political rhetoric ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Comrade Ini Ememobong, on Tuesday, the INWC demanded that Tinubu publicly renounce his previous remarks, which it accused of encouraging hostility towards opposition parties. The statement cited Tinubu’s 2022 declaration that political power must be “grabbed, snatched and run away with”, as well as his 2026 remark that “all is fair in politics”, as examples of what it described as dangerous political messaging. “These two statements alone, coming from their leader, were the adrenaline that APC followers needed to unleash unmitigated mayhem on opposition parties,” it alleged. It also cited alleged threats by some APC figures, including Senator Fadahunsi of Osun State, the Chairman of Kuje Area Council and the party’s Edo State chairman, against citizens unwilling to vote for the ruling party. On Delta State, the group alleged that intimidation of opposition figures had become recurrent, claiming that at least two deadly attacks against opposition groups had occurred in November alone. It further alleged that the incidents were widely believed to have been sponsored by the APC. “With this latest attack and the deaths and injuries it caused, the world can now clearly see the fruits of the evil seed planted by the APC through violent communication,” the statement said. The INWC also demanded a thorough and transparent investigation into the attack, urging the police to make their findings public. It called on the Inspector-General of Police to ensure that the investigation he ordered was conducted professionally and that other political attacks across the country received similar attention. It urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), the National Peace Committee and election observers to identify and publicly expose individuals responsible for political violence, including through international platforms. The group also raised concerns over allegations that police personnel were present at the scene but failed to assist victims, calling on security agencies, particularly the police, to demonstrate neutrality and professionalism. “Nigerians need responsible leadership that does not sacrifice the peace and unity of the country at the altar of political domination and elections,” it said.

item.description: Bitcoin Magazine South Korea Unveils Crypto Bill Capping Exchange Ownership at 20% South Korea’s Financial Services Commission on Tuesday unveiled a government bill that would cap a major shareholder’s stake in a crypto exchange at 20%, open the door to domestic coin offerings and let bank-led groups issue won stablecoins. The draft, titled the Act on the Innovation of the Digital Asset Industry and Protection of Users, was presented at a Virtual Asset Committee meeting chaired by FSC Chairman Lee Eog-weon. It would replace Korea’s two-track system, built on an anti-money-laundering law and a 2024 user protection act, with a single framework covering the industry, markets and users. Lee said the law would raise trust and transparency in Korea’s digital asset market and help draw new money into the industry. He said the government would do everything it can to see the bill fully debated in the National Assembly and enacted quickly. A 20% ownership cap for exchanges Under the bill, exchanges would become “digital asset platform operators,” a designation reserved for firms that hold separate licenses for dealing, brokerage and custody. The FSC modeled the ownership limit on the rules for alternative trading systems in the stock market. Major shareholders could own up to 20%, or up to 34% with FSC approval under a presidential decree. Shares above the limit would lose their voting rights. Existing exchanges would get three years after designation to comply, and small and midsize exchanges could get up to three more. The cap could reach some of Korea’s best-known exchanges. Mirae Asset Consulting owns 97.15% of Digital X, the exchange formerly known as Korbit, The Korea Herald reported . Naver Financial’s planned share-swap takeover of Dunamu, the operator of Upbit, would make the exchange a wholly owned subsidiary. The FSC declined to comment on specific companies, the paper said. “Ownership restrictions are necessary to strengthen exchanges’ public accountability and neutrality,” Yoo Young-jun, director general of the FSC’s Digital Financial Policy Bureau, said at a briefing, citing more than 10 million exchange accounts in Korea. The bill would also move trade execution, listing reviews and market surveillance from self-regulation to formal rules. Exchanges would need outside directors to make up a majority of their boards, plus audit committees and compliance officers. item.title: NYSC warns Bayelsa corps members against night movements, politicians
item.description: By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa The National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) in Bayelsa State has warned corps members deployed to the state to avoid late-night movements, compromising situations and unnecessary exposure to security risks. The State Coordinator, Mr Samuel Pepple, gave the warning on Tuesday during the low-key closing ceremony of the 2026 Batch C Stream II orientation course at the NYSC Permanent Orientation Camp, Boro Town, Kolokuma-Opokuma Local Government Area. Pepple urged the departing corps members to uphold discipline, remain security-conscious and demonstrate integrity as they proceed to their respective Places of Primary Assignment (PPAs). He advised them to embrace their postings, particularly those assigned to rural and riverine communities, assuring them of adequate security arrangements, decent accommodation and necessary safety equipment, including life jackets for those deployed to riverine areas. On electoral responsibilities, Pepple warned them against political interference, inducements and other actions capable of compromising their integrity. He stressed that corps members must remain politically neutral and discharge any electoral responsibilities assigned to them with professionalism and patriotism. He noted that their services were particularly needed in rural and riverine communities, where access to essential services, especially education, remained limited. item.title: DOJ Moves to Forfeit $1.1 Billion in USDC Stolen in Binance Hack
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine DOJ Moves to Forfeit $1.1 Billion in USDC Stolen in Binance Hack The Justice Department filed a civil forfeiture complaint Monday to take ownership of more than $1.1 billion in USDC that North Korean hackers stole from Binance last month, tokens that Circle froze but says it cannot move. The complaint , filed in U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia, targets all USDC held at 36 addresses across 18 blockchains. The department said the U.S. has now helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9 billion in crypto from multiple sources since the Oct. 29 theft. On Nov. 12, the department said it had court authority to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion, out of a joint government and industry freeze of more than $2.7 billion. A temporary restraining order issued that day was served on Circle the same day. Monday’s filing is the step that would let the government take title to the funds. Circle will mint replacement tokens Circle blocked access to the USDC on or about Oct. 29, the complaint says. But the stablecoin issuer told prosecutors it does not have the technical ability to transfer the tokens out of the blocklisted addresses, which remain under the hackers’ control. Instead, Circle has agreed to issue new USDC equal to the frozen amount and send it to the U.S. once a court enters a forfeiture order. The complaint calls those tokens “Substitute USDC.” Several of the addresses are smart contract and hot wallet addresses on Binance’s own platform. The hackers took them over in the attack and drained some, but not all, of the funds before Circle stepped in, prosecutors wrote. “It appears Binance no longer controlled them,” the complaint says. How the Binance hack worked The filing also lays out how investigators say the breach began. A Binance employee contacted by a purported recruiter agreed to a job interview and was told to download software that contained malware, which matches what the exchange said earlier this month. The infected device let the attackers plant an EIP-7702 injection. That feature, added to Ethereum in a 2025 upgrade, lets ordinary wallets temporarily act like smart contracts. Prosecutors said the hackers used it to take control of Binance’s hot wallets and route funds to a “sweeper” contract that moved them out as soon as they arrived. The first large transfer, about $780 million in USDC, left Binance on Ethereum at about 4:41 p.m. ET on Oct. 29, the complaint says. Another $43 million followed 18 minutes later. Investigators also traced AVAX that was split up, bridged and swapped until it became about $1.56 million in USDC. U.S. agencies attribute the theft to North Korean military hackers known as the Lazarus Group, or APT38. item.title: 2027: Atiku storms Kogi, says Nigerians deserve to live with dignity
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar on Tuesday took his campaign to Kogi State, declaring that Nigerians should be able to live with dignity in their own country. At a rally, supporters reportedly chanted ‘Tinubu Must Go!’ as Atiku criticised the economic hardship facing households, traders and workers, and called for a change in the country’s economic direction. In a statement by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku said the reception in Kogi reflected the frustration of families struggling to cope with rising living costs. “They came here in their numbers because they want to be heard. Their hardship is real, and their hope deserves an answer,” he said. Atiku said his proposed economic approach would focus on reducing fuel costs, supporting local production and ensuring that Nigerians could get more value from their earnings. “A mother should not have to choose between feeding her children and paying their school fees. A trader should not open a shop each morning wondering whether anyone can afford to buy. A young person should not work hard all day and still struggle to pay for the journey home. These are the lives behind the figures this government recites,” he said. Explaining his campaign’s promise of affordable living, Atiku said the objective was to make it easier for ordinary Nigerians to meet their daily needs. “When we say we will make life affordable again, we are speaking to the parent counting the last notes in a purse and the worker calculating whether a salary will last until month’s end,” he said. Reacting to the chants against President Bola Tinubu, Atiku said they reflected the frustration of people who felt they had been asked to endure hardship without a clear end in sight. “The people of Kogi are chanting ‘Tinubu Must Go’ because they are tired of being told to endure pain with no end in sight. I hear them. I see the faces in this crowd, and I know what is at stake. No family should have to beg for the chance to live with dignity in its own country,” he said. He thanked the people of Kogi for their reception and urged his supporters to remain peaceful, while encouraging them to use their votes to determine the country’s political future. “Let no one mistake your restraint for acceptance of hardship. item.title: Relai Launches Stacks, Letting Bitcoin Savers Split Plans by Goal
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Relai Launches Stacks, Letting Bitcoin Savers Split Plans by Goal Swiss bitcoin app Relai launched Stacks on Tuesday, a feature that lets users run several recurring bitcoin savings plans side by side, one for each goal, such as a house, a wedding or a child’s first car. Stacks is live for all Relai users in Switzerland and the European Union. Each Stack carries its own amount and schedule, and users can change either at any time without starting over, the company said. A savings plan is Relai’s version of dollar-cost averaging: buying a fixed amount of bitcoin on a set schedule, weekly or monthly, regardless of price. Savers use it to avoid timing the market. Since September, Relai users have been able to change the amount and buy date of an active plan. Stacks applies that to several goals at once, so a saver can put more toward a house one month, slow down a car fund the next and leave an emergency reserve untouched. In practice, Stacks is an organizing layer, not a new account. Relai’s help pages describe each Stack as a separate pot with its own bitcoin address inside the same wallet. Users get up to five custom Stacks plus a main balance, and moving bitcoin between them takes a regular on-chain transaction with a network fee. Self-custody cuts both ways Relai is self-custodial, meaning it does not hold customers’ bitcoin. The coins in every Stack sit in a wallet controlled by a 12-word recovery phrase, or seed phrase, that only the user has. All Stacks share that one phrase, and restoring the wallet with it brings every Stack back. The trade-off is responsibility. A saver who loses the phrase and the phone has no password reset and no support desk that can recover the coins. Anyone who gets the phrase can take them, which is why attackers have gone as far as tampering with hardware wallets to capture it. “Everyone saves for something. A home, their kids, the freedom to stop working one day,” said Julian Liniger, Relai’s co-founder and CEO. “With Stacks, you can save for each of those goals in Bitcoin, at your own pace.” How Relai is regulated In the EU, Relai’s French unit is authorized by France’s financial markets regulator, the AMF, as a crypto-asset service provider under MiCA, the bloc’s Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation . Relai secured that license in October 2025, and under MiCA a firm licensed in one member state can “passport” its services across the bloc. Swiss and Liechtenstein customers are served by Relai AG, which is affiliated with VQF , a self-regulatory organization recognized by Swiss regulator FINMA under the country’s anti-money laundering law. Goal-based saving in bitcoin also carries price risk that a bank savings account does not. item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Slips to $60,000 as November ETF Outflows Hit Record The bitcoin price slipped back to near $60,000 early Tuesday, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data, as the Nvidia-fueled rally in stocks cooled and spot bitcoin ETFs posted another heavy day of outflows. item.title: Trump gains possibly millions from Nvidia shares after Huang’s return – Report
item.description: The spectacular rebound in Nvidia’s share price following Jensen Huang’s return as chief executive could have added as much as $15 million to US President Donald Trump’s holdings in the stock on Monday, according to calculations by the Financial Times. Huang resigned on November 12 over extramarital affairs including one with a suspected Chinese spy, a departure that sent shares in the US chip giant tumbling. News of his return sent Nvidia shares soaring more than 30 percent and added more than $900 billion to the company’s market value. According to the Financial Times, Trump may have owned as many as 370,000 shares in Nvidia as of September 30. The newspaper based its estimate on the president’s financial disclosures to the Office of Government Ethics, the most recent of which was filed on November 5. The disclosures do not include precise figures for disposals and purchases of shares. The maximum figure for his holdings was therefore calculated on the assumption of purchases at the upper limit of each range, and sales at the lower limit. A report from ABC News, citing Trump’s annual financial disclosure report, did not specify the number of shares he owned but said their value reached at least $12 million by the end of 2025. It added that his accounts have continued to trade Nvidia in recent months, citing separate filings. Nvidia said Monday that it had reinstated Huang as chief executive after receiving information from the US government that he did not pose a national security risk. Trump said Huang’s return followed his own direct contacts with Nvidia’s board. “I’ve been speaking to the board directly and indirectly, and I felt very strongly about it,” he told US broadcaster CNBC. item.title: Peter Obi Lacks Competence To Lead Nigeria, Tinubu 100% Better — Abure
item.description: Former National Chairman of the Labour Party, Julius Abure, has said the party’s former presidential candidate, Peter Obi, lacks the character and competence to lead Nigeria, insisting that President Bola Tinubu is “100 per cent better”. Abure said he would not support Obi’s presidential ambition in the 2027 general election, citing his experience working with the former Anambra State governor and the internal crisis that fractured the Labour Party. He made the remarks during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today , where he explained why he considered Tinubu a better choice among the leading contenders for the presidency. Abure was a key ally of Obi during the 2023 presidential campaign and campaigned extensively for him. However, Obi subsequently left the Labour Party following a protracted leadership crisis. He blamed Obi’s caretaker committee decision for deepening the Labour Party’s crisis, driving elected officials away and raising questions about his leadership. “If indeed Obi was a good leader, why did they not follow Peter Obi? Peter Obi doesn’t have the character and competence to lead the country; we are sorry to say. Given my experience, I now know better,” he said. Peter Obi and Julius Abure appear in court for the presidential election petitions tribunal on Friday, June 2, 2023 Asked whether his decision to campaign extensively for Obi in 2023 had been a mistake, Abure admitted that it might have been. “Yes, it may have been an error because I now know better. Experience, they say, is the best teacher. Now I have experienced working with Peter Obi and that he is unstable, unreliable, a pretender who cannot be trusted because of the way he treated the leadership of the party,” he said. ﻿ Asked whether he still considered Obi “a saint,” Abure declared his support for Tinubu, describing the president as a more suitable candidate. “President Bola Tinubu is 100 per cent better. Today, we have the right to support whatever candidate we want. Obviously, Peter Obi is out of the question for us to support, given our experiences with him. We made a critical analysis of all the candidates: Tinubu, Atiku and Obi. “We feel Tinubu is the best candidate for us to support, given his trajectory so far in office and his ability to resolve conflicts compared to Peter Obi. The stage we are in now requires someone who can bring people together because the country is more divided than ever before. We need a bridge-builder who can unite people, and I do not believe Peter Obi has that capacity at this critical time in our history,” he said. He, however, dismissed allegations that he was responsible for Obi’s departure from the Labour Party, describing such claims as a “clear misconception”. item.title: Amazon says hackers' AI agents found and exploited 0-day with little human input
item.description: Amazon said AI agents recently found and exploited a zero-day vulnerability with no human oversight beyond a simple instruction to get root access on an East Asian university server. The agents were running on Cairn, an open source AI penetration-testing framework. The hackers, who provided prompts in simplified Chinese and configured the model to the Chinese Standard Time zone, gave the agents a list of IP addresses and the goal: “obtain shell access.” In short order, the agents discovered a zero-day in an open source medical imaging AI application running on one of the target servers. The agents then exploited the vulnerability and gained full control of the system. “These findings show that agentic offensive operations are already happening, and defenders should prepare for the speed and persistence these tools enable,” Amazon said . item.title: One terminal command gave my forgotten Android device a desk job
item.description: My kitchen junk drawer used to hold takeout menus and coupons, but it has since become a storage spot for old tablets or phones. Like me, you probably have a few devices lying around that are perfectly functional but don't meet your daily driving needs. It's tucked out of view, living out its life in a drawer until being erased and donated after someone asks why you're holding onto outdated, unused devices. Thankfully, PhoneBox has a solution. You weren't hoarding old tech; you were waiting for the proper use. The PhoneBox home screen displays useful stats and what's currently playing in your browser. Credit: Nick Indge I had an old AllDoCube iPlay 50 mini Pro 8.4-inch tablet that seemed like the perfect candidate. I bought the tablet second-hand as a possible big-screen gaming and emulation tablet to use with a telescopic control deck, but I quickly found I vastly preferred just using a dedicated device. Since that realization, this decent little unit has lived its life in "the drawer." Launch applications on your PC from the connected Android device. Credit: Nick Indge Installation is a doddle Getting PhoneBox up and running on my tablet and PC couldn't have been simpler. After making sure that the Android tablet was in developer mode, the process was as easy as plugging the tablet in to my PC via USB and executing a single copied command in my Linux terminal. The script downloaded the PhoneBox 0.9.29 software for my PC, verified the downloaded checksum against the release, and walked me through a few quick Y/N installation questions. The script offers to create a systemd user service, so the desktop agent launches after initial login, and even asks if you'd like it to install the PhoneBox APK to your connected Android device. item.title: How Williams Alamu Graduated with First-Class Honours in Statistics from the University of Ibadan
item.description: Williams Alamu marks his B.Sc. First-Class Honours graduation in Statistics from the University of Ibadan. There was a time when Williams Alamu would rather not sit an examination than risk getting a grade he wasn’t happy with. A B or a C in his Cambridge A-levels felt like a possibility he wasn’t ready to entertain, so he didn’t write the exams. A few years later, at 23, he has graduated from the University of Ibadan with a B.Sc. in Statistics, First-Class Honours and a CGPA of 3.65/4.0. Somewhere along the way, he decided that fear was no longer going to make his decisions for him. When Williams got into UI, he had a rather ambitious plan: become the Best Graduating Student in his faculty. Getting there would require more than good intentions. There were 5:30am wake-ups, difficult Statistics courses, friends who became unofficial tutors, a ChatGPT Pro subscription in 300 level, job offers he turned down and one Demography exam that kept him awake for 36 hours. University, as it turns out, came with quite a few plot twists. In this interview with BellaNaija, Williams takes us through the habits, people and decisions that shaped his academic journey. He also tells us whether he got that coveted top spot, what he learnt from the opportunities he put on hold, and what he would tell another student hoping to graduate with First-Class Honours. If that’s a goal you’re working towards, you may want to take notes. Literally or otherwise. Williams Alamu celebrates graduating with First-Class Honours in Statistics from the University of Ibadan. At what point did you realise you were chasing a record-breaking grade? Was it a goal from Day 1, or did it evolve? It was a goal from day one, actually. When I gained admission into the University of Ibadan, I already had my mind set on graduating as the Best Graduating Student in my faculty. I knew becoming the overall Best Graduating Student in the university would require an extraordinary amount of work, but I felt being the best in my faculty was something I wanted to work towards. And, of course, that would also mean graduating as the best student in my department. The motivation behind that goal goes back to shortly after secondary school, when my parents enrolled me in a Cambridge A-level programme. I went into it hoping to achieve three A-stars, but Chemistry was a major struggle. As the examinations approached, I became increasingly worried about my performance. I think I was more afraid of not meeting my own expectations than I was of the examination itself. The thought of getting a B or C frightened me so much that I eventually decided not to sit for the examinations. item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. On Friday, Kuntz was already speaking of the team in the past tense. “I really enjoyed my time at the Galaxy. I love being here,” he said. “I’d like to be back if it was up to me. item.title: Severe eczema healed by novel immune-calming pill in clinical trial
item.description: Eczema causes itchy, inflamed rashes on the skin Evgeniia Gordeeva/Getty Images Over a third of people with moderate to severe eczema taking part in a clinical trial have seen their skin completely or almost completely clear up after taking an experimental pill for four months. The drug targets a part of the immune system that causes eczema when it gets stuck in overdrive, and it may be preferable to the current standard treatment, which has to be injected. “It definitely looks promising,” says Gayle Ross at the Royal Melbourne Hospital. Read more Chronic inflammation messes with your mind. Here’s how to calm it Eczema, or atopic dermatitis, is a chronic skin condition characterised by itchy, inflamed rashes and broken skin that can become infected. It is driven by an overactive immune pathway involving two signalling proteins called interleukin-4 and interleukin-13. Advertisement In 2017, the companies Sanofi and Regeneron received approval in the US for their jointly developed eczema drug dupilumab, which blocks interleukin-4 and interleukin-13 signalling. But, although the medication is effective , it has had limited uptake in the US because it must be injected under the skin and costs up to $59,000 per year for those without insurance coverage. Now, another company, Kymera Therapeutics, has developed an alternative treatment that can be taken in pill form, called KT-621. It targets the same immune pathway as dupilumab but degrades a protein called STAT6 that is activated downstream from interleukin-4 and interleukin-13 in the development of eczema. Free newsletter Sign up to Health Check Sign up to newsletter In the clinical trial , 244 adults with an average age of 39 and moderate to severe eczema were randomised to take KT-621 at three different doses or a placebo pill every day for 16 weeks. Those taking the most effective dose experienced an average 72 per cent reduction in their eczema severity on a standard scale, compared to 27 per cent in the placebo group. What’s more, 38 per cent of participants taking KT-621 had completely healed skin or almost completely healed skin by the end of the trial. “These results exceeded our expectations,” said Terence Rooney , the chief medical officer of Kymera Therapeutics, when announcing the results in a webcast on 23 November. He showed before-and-after photos of one man who had had severe eczema all over his torso at the beginning of the trial, which disappeared by the end. “It’s obviously early days and the trial had relatively small patient numbers, but [KT-621] looks like it has similar efficacy to dupilumab, which is currently the standard of care for moderate to severe atopic dermatitis, and it would be nice to have an oral option as opposed to an injection,” says Ross. item.title: ‎After Daily Trust story, foundation sponsors surgery for Kano teen battling facial tumour
item.description: ‎The Ihsan Scholarship Foundation, Kano, has sponsored the life-changing surgery of Salisu Sani, an 18-year-old whose struggle with a debilitating facial tumour was highlighted by Daily Trust, restoring hope to the teenager and offering him a chance to rebuild his future. ‎‎Daily Trust had reported how Salisu Sani, an indigene of Yalwa town in Tofa Local Government Area of Kano State, spent his days along Gandun Albasa Street in Kano soliciting support for a critical surgery after a massive tumour on his face left him in constant pain and threatened his eyesight. ‎‎Following the publication, a Kano-based foundation known for its humanitarian and educational interventions reached out to the teenager and took over the responsibility of his treatment. ‎The foundation, which requested anonymity, facilitated his return to the [Aminu Kano Teaching Hospital (AKTH), where medical evaluations were conducted and the much-needed surgery was successfully carried out. ‎Medical records obtained by Daily Trust showed that specialists at the hospital diagnosed the condition as Aggressive Trabecular Ossifying Fibroma, a rare fibro-osseous tumour affecting the jaw and facial bones. ‎The pathology report indicated that tissue samples removed during surgery weighed about 640 grams. ‎‎Family members expressed gratitude to the foundation, medical personnel and members of the public who showed concern after the story was published. ‎Speaking after the successful operation, Salisu Sani said the intervention had given him a new lease of life. ‎“I never imagined that help would come this fast. For years I lived with the pain and the burden of carrying this tumour on my face. Today, I feel hopeful again,” he said. ‎The teenager had earlier told Daily Trust that the illness had forced him out of school and shattered his dreams, as his family could not afford the cost of treatment. ‎In a further boost to his recovery and future, the foundation also pledged to support his long-term rehabilitation by either sponsoring his education or providing him with full startup capital to establish a business and become self-reliant. ‎‎A representative of the foundation said the decision was informed by the need to ensure that the teenager not only receives medical care but also has the opportunity to build a productive life after recovery. ‎‎“Our concern is not limited to the surgery alone. We want him to be able to stand on his own feet and pursue his dreams. Whether through formal education or entrepreneurship, we will support him to become self-reliant,” the representative said.

item.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Eruption Extends Iwo Jima’s… Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search October 26 November 11 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison October 26 November 11 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison October 26 November 11 Curtain Toggle 2-Up A volcanic eruption in the shallows near Iwo Jima has extended the Japanese island’s famed black sand beaches, at least temporarily. Signs of unrest began in late October 2026. On October 27, seismic sensors recorded a sharp uptick in activity, and Japan’s Meteorological Agency reported that the first photographs of the eruption were captured. Soon after, sensors on several satellites began to capture an array of observations. The OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 captured the left image on October 26, when the coast was still quiet. On November 11, Landsat 9 got its first clear view of the land the submarine volcano has built (right). A shortwave-infrared signature, a sign of the eruption’s heat, is shown in orange. A faint gray volcanic plume drifts southeast of the vent, and a streak of floating pumice stretches across the water in the same direction. A false-color backscatter radar image from the NISAR (NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar) satellite offered an even earlier look at the eruption. On October 28, despite heavy cloud cover, the radar detected a large disturbance in the water in the same area that erupted in December 2023. When the clouds cleared in early November, the MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) and VIIRS (Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite) sensors on NASA and NOAA satellites also captured signs of the ongoing eruption’s volcanic plumes and infrared signature . Japan’s Coast Guard released a report on November 16 confirming the formation of new land connected to the pre-existing beach. The eruption appears to have added roughly 50 hectares (125 acres) of new beach, about the area of 90 American football fields. That would enlarge the island by about 1.7 percent. The new land adjoins the southeast beach where American troops landed on February 19, 1945, beginning one of the bloodiest battles in the history of the U.S. Marines. The location of the eruption is no surprise to scientists. In addition to the 2023 eruption off the southeast coast, Iwo Jima had an eruption off its west coast in August 2025, said Daniel Slayback, a scientist at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center. Trump claimed that the fate of the unstable, highly explosive material is now in the hands of a federal court and Rob Sand, Iowa's governor-elect, who won't be sworn into office until January. The Army had planned to detonate the barrels on November 20, but delayed the blast on Thursday amid public outcry and a legal challenge from environmental groups. The explosion will launch a plume of toxic gases and neurotoxic lead that could reach up to 100 miles away from the Iowa facility, the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP). Iowa residents and officials said they learned of the detonation only days beforehand.
